word.title: Element Fits Schema
word.description: A node's fully realized tapestryJson fits the JSON schema of each concept it is an element of.

graphRule.name: element-fits-schema
graphRule.says: a node's fully realized tapestryJson fits the JSON schema of each concept it is an element of. This is BIBLE §10's rule 4, "Elements MUST validate against their concept's JSON Schema", and the owner's D9: each node is an element of at least one concept, and must validate against the format that concept expects. A concept's schema describes a node's tapestryJson, the JSON the Tapestry LMDB (the tapestry-store, not strfry's LMDB) holds for it: its word block, a section for each concept it is an element of, and its `graphContext` (ADR graph-operations-first-slice/0020a). A node belongs to every concept whose class thread reaches it (rule 3), so a node in a set that two concepts' class threads reach has two schemas to fit. A schema is read one way, by the one check both readers use (`src/operations/catalog/graph/_schemas.js`): the JSON schema node's `jsonSchema` section, its `$schema` dropped, checked with ajv's defaults, which read draft-07's keywords. The rule and the derive step judge the same document, against the same concepts, so they give one verdict; the derive step keeps a dated copy of it in each node's `graphContext.parentJsonSchemas`, and the rule decides when it is asked (ADR graph-operations-first-slice/0042). A node's tapestryJson can be missing, incomplete or out of date, and the rule speaks of its fully realized form. Exceptions to the rule, for performance, will come; none is written yet (ADR 0020a, Decision 2).
graphRule.kind: a graph rule, about the owner's and the admins' own element writes (D4). As a check it judges every element by where it came from (D15): an element an import brought in is reported, never refused.
graphRule.refusesOrReports:
it refuses the write, before anything changes:
- `invalid-fields` (400) when the JSON the write builds doesn't fit the concept's schema. The refusal lists every problem, each naming the field and what is wrong: a required field left out, a value of the wrong type, a value the schema doesn't allow, a field the schema doesn't take. It names at most twenty, then how many more. No value is made up for a field left out;
- `no-schema` (409) when the concept's schema is missing, can't be read, or doesn't compile, so nothing could be checked. The refusal says why.

A write judges its JSON before the derive step has built the node's `graphContext`, so it sets aside every problem that is only about `graphContext`: a concept the JSON misses for nothing else is reported as waiting for the derive step, and the write isn't refused for it; a concept it misses for other things too is refused, or reported, for those alone (ADR 0042, Decision 3). An element in a set may join other concepts too. The write reports whether its JSON fits each of their schemas, or waits, and doesn't refuse for them: giving the element their sections is `graph add-to-concept` (A10.22).
graphRule.check: the same `violations` over a set of nodes, each as `{ node }`, judges each node's tapestryJson as the tapestry-store holds it, and names each node and each concept whose schema it doesn't fit, and each concept with no schema to check against; as `{ node, concept }` it judges against the one named. Nothing is set aside: tapestryJson without its `graphContext` doesn't fit `word`'s schema. A node with no tapestryJson yet is named once, its finding marked `missing`, so a report can tell a node not yet built from one that doesn't fit; tapestryJson that isn't an object is named once too. A finding on a tapestryJson that has its `graphContext` gives when it was built, its `derivedAt`, since an entry built before a change is judged as it is (ADR 0020a, Decision 5). `rules check` (A10.31) will run it over the graph. The property operations (A10.18) will run it over a concept's elements after its schema changes, reporting only.
graphRule.repair: none yet. `graph update-node` (A10.21) changes an element's fields, and `graph add-to-concept` (A10.22) gives it another concept's section.
graphRule.enforcedBy: the guard of `graph create-element`, run in its write once it has taken the lock on the concept's header and built the element's JSON, since that JSON comes from the graph. The rule's code is in `src/operations/rules/element-fits-schema.js`. The check it uses is in `src/operations/catalog/graph/_schemas.js`, which `graph create-set`, `graph update-node`, `graph add-to-concept` and the derive step (`src/lib/derivers/schema-verdicts.js`) call too, and the property operations (A10.18) will call when they are built. Built in story graph-operations-first-slice #20 (ADR graph-operations-first-slice/0020), and made to judge tapestryJson in story #42 (ADR graph-operations-first-slice/0042).
